title: Preity Zinta Has Launched a Luxury Polki Jewellery Brand. Her Partners Include a Mafatlal Heir and a Dubai Luxury Group.
excerpt: Jacarti Jewellery opened its Bandra flagship on June 4 with Bobby Deol and Celina Jaitly in attendance. The brand is betting on a new Polki art form it calls Merai.
body:
Preity Zinta has launched Jacarti Jewellery, a luxury fine jewellery brand specialising in Polki pieces, with a flagship store now open on Waterfield Road in Bandra, Mumbai. The brand is a joint venture with Samara Punjabi of the Timeless Group in the UAE and Priyavrata Mafatlal, Vice-Chairman of the Arvind Mafatlal Group — bringing together Bollywood star power, Gulf-based luxury retail experience, and one of India's oldest industrial families.

The launch event on June 4 drew Bobby Deol, Celina Jaitly, and Iulia Vantur, among others. Celina posted from the event, calling the collection "absolutely phenomenal — elegant, distinctive, and truly out of this world" and encouraging jewellery enthusiasts to visit the Bandra store.

## What Jacarti Is Selling

The brand positions itself around Polki — uncut diamond jewellery that has been central to Indian bridal and heirloom traditions for centuries. Where most Polki houses lean heavily on traditional design, Jacarti is introducing what it calls *Merai*, a proprietary art form that the founders describe as "a new age of Polki" — blending heritage craftsmanship with contemporary design language.

The pitch is aimed at a specific consumer: someone who wants jewellery that feels culturally rooted but doesn't look like it was pulled from a family vault. Think Sabyasachi's approach to bridal wear, applied to Polki diamonds.

Jacarti is available both through the physical store and via e-commerce at jacarti.com, signalling an intention to reach buyers beyond Mumbai from the start.

## Why This Matters for NRIs

The Indian diaspora is one of the largest markets for Indian fine jewellery, and Polki in particular has seen a resurgence among younger NRI brides and collectors who want pieces that connect them to Indian craft traditions. The involvement of Samara Punjabi's Timeless Group, which operates in the UAE luxury market, suggests that Gulf and international expansion is part of the plan from day one.

For decades, NRIs have relied on family connections or trips home to source high-quality Polki. A brand with e-commerce capability, a recognisable face, and the industrial backing of the Mafatlal Group could simplify that process — if the product delivers on its premium positioning.

## Preity Zinta's Business Portfolio

This is not Zinta's first venture outside cinema. She co-owns the Punjab Kings (formerly Kings XI Punjab) in the IPL — a franchise she acquired with her husband Gene Goodenough and Ness Wadia. The jewellery brand adds a luxury retail dimension to a portfolio that already spans entertainment and sports.

At 51, Zinta has been largely absent from the screen in recent years, with her last significant role being in the 2018 film *Bhaiaji Superhit*. The Jacarti launch positions her firmly in the entrepreneur space, joining a growing list of Bollywood actors — including Anushka Sharma (Nush), Deepika Padukone (82°E), and Masaba Gupta (House of Masaba) — who have built businesses that leverage their public profile without depending on film roles.

## The Competitive Landscape

The Indian luxury jewellery market has become increasingly crowded, with brands like Sabyasachi Fine Jewellery, Tanishq's luxury lines, and established Polki houses like Birdhichand Ghanshyamdas all competing for the same high-net-worth consumer. Jacarti's differentiator will need to be more than celebrity association — it will need to prove that its *Merai* technique and design philosophy offer something that existing Polki brands do not.

The early signals — a Bandra flagship, e-commerce from launch, cross-border founding partners, and a curated celebrity launch — suggest the founders are aware of the stakes. Whether it becomes a lasting brand or a celebrity-endorsed boutique will depend on what happens after the launch party ends.
